Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City HAROLD P. ABBAS Secretary to the Sanggunian http: //www.dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION No. s. 2018 Sangguniang Bayan of Loreto, Agusan del Sur Office of the Sangguniang Bayan Secretary Brgy. Poblacion, Loreto, Agusan del Sur Dear Mr. Abbas: 22 AUG This has reference to your Indorsement dated 12 March 2018 of Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 478-2028 requesting for this Department's opinion on the validity of Municipal Ordinance No. 032-2017 after it was returned by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Per the Sangguniang Resolution No. 478-2028 and other pertinent documents presented, enacted Municipal Ordinance No. 032-2017 submitted to the Municipal Mayoron 27 October 2018 was returned unsigned and recommended for further evaluation and deliberation only on 28 November 2017. There being no valid veto, it was deemed approved by the Sangguniang Bayan and was submitted for review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. It was, however, returned by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan with the information that "the August Body cannot treat this ordinance in the absence of a resolution overriding the veto of the municipal mayor". Hence, the request for opinion on the validity of the subject municipal ordinance. The Department opines that Municipal Ordinance No. 032-2017 shall be deemed consistent with law and therefore valid. First, there is no valid veto communicated by the LCE within the prescribed IO-day period. Section 55 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ", provides as follows: "Section 55. Veto Power of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) The local chief executive may veto any ordinance of the sanggunian panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sanggunian bayan on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare, stating his reasons therefor in writing.

(b) The local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall have the power to veto any-particular item or items ofan appropriations ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability. In such a case, the veto shall not affect the item or items which are not objected to. The vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the sanggunian overrides the veto in the manner herein provided; otherwise, the item or items in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed reenacted. (c) The local chief executive may veto an ordinance or resolution only once. The sanggunian may override the veto of the local chiefexecutive concerned by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without the approval of the local chief executive concerned. " Herein, the Municipal Ordiance No. 478-2028 was merely returned unsigned for further assessment and deliberation, not based on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare. Hence, there is no veto to override with. The Ordinance having been correctly considered as "deemed approved as if the LCE had signed it", it was properly submitted for review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Second, the action of returning the subject ordinance by reason of "absence ofa resolution overriding the veto of the municipal mayor" is not a valid action of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan concerned in the concept of Section 56 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ", which states: "Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Pamala wigan. (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies ofsuch ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period often (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing of his comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang panlalawigan in making its decision.

(c) Ifthe sangguniangpanlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sanguniang panlungsod or sarwmiang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangruniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken. (d) If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission ofsuch an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. " (Emphasis Supplied) "The Sangguniang Panlalawigan is required to take action on the ordinance on review thirty (30) days after its submission. This Department had consistently opined that the phrase "take action" should be construed as either approval or disapproval of the ordinance and not just any other action of the reviewing sanggunian, such as referral to a committee. After the lapse of such period, and no official and/or formal document, such as a resolution which shall contain the findings of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on review of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Ordinance, was issued by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, it can be validly stated that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan failed to act within thirty (30) days and the ordinance or resolution under review can be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. "1 In the herein case, the action taken by the concerned Sangguniang Panlalawigan does not constitute an approval nor a disapproval in whole or in part of the Ordinance submitted for review. It is as if no action has been taken thereon which gave way to the application of the last paragraph of the aforecited provision, the ordinance shall be deemed consistent with law and therefore valid. This opinion is hereby being rendered without prejudice to contrary opinions from competent authorities or ruling of proper courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very y yours, By auth ty the ecretary: A. PANADERO Undersecretary LILIBEI'H A FAMACION, 111 Regional Director, DILG Region XIII DILG Opinion No. 19 s. 2009 dated 28 April 2009.
